Create a hexamap (eAppendix interface)

Source: R/compat.R
create_hexamap.Rd

Wrapper around hexamap() that keeps the argument names used in the eAppendix of Jalal and Burke (2020), so published code runs unchanged. It uses the "jet" palette of the paper by default. New code should call hexamap() directly.

Usage

create_hexamap(
  data,
  first_age,
  first_period,
  interval,
  color_scale = NULL,
  palette = "jet",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) with ages as rows and periods as columns. Missing and non-finite cells are not drawn.

first_age

First age in data. Defaults to the first row name of data, if numeric.

first_period

First period in data. Defaults to the first column name of data, if numeric.

interval

Width of the age and period groups, which must be equal. Defaults to the spacing of the numeric row or column names of data, or 1.

color_scale

Numeric vector of length 2 with the lower and upper limits of the color scale. Passed to colorbar_range in hexamap().

palette

Palette name passed to hexamap(). Defaults to "jet", as in the paper.

...

Further arguments passed to hexamap().

Value

The hexamap_layout object returned by hexamap_layout(), invisibly.

Examples

rates <- outer(15:70, 1999:2018, function(a, p) (a - 10) * (p - 1990) / 40)
create_hexamap(data = rates,
               first_age = 15,
               first_period = 1999,
               interval = 1,
               first_age_isoline = 20,
               first_period_isoline = 2000,
               isoline_interval = 10,
               color_scale = c(0, 40))
